function: Designs the BS partially-connected hybrid beamforming (analog phase-shifter matrix and digital precoder) to maximize downlink sum rate, scalable to user and RF chain numbers (p. 3-7).
system: BS with Nt = N x M antennas (M RF chains, partially-connected phase shifters), K single-antenna users; K=3-7, M=4-8, N=4-8; mmWave, carrier not stated; no RIS (p. 3, 10-11).
method: Bipartite GNN with four shared MLP vertex operators (3 layers, 200 hidden units, R=2 iterations); unsupervised training maximizing sum rate with Adam, cosine-annealed learning rate (p. 6-8, 10).
data_channel: Custom Saleh-Valenzuela mmWave channel: 5 clusters, 2 paths, Laplacian AoD with 7.5 degree spread, ULA; channels generated per mini-batch for training; test data not described (p. 3, 8).
test_conditions: Fixed K, M: Pt sweep (-20 to 5 dB), N sweep (4-8). Scalability: model trained over M in {4..8} or K in {3..7}, tested at those values (p. 10-11).
baselines: Non-learned: SDP-AltMin [10], MM-AltMin [12], Element-AltMax [18]. Learned: conventional DNN, a 3-layer MLP on the vectorized channel (p. 9).
metrics: Achievable sum rate (bps/Hz) versus Pt, N, M and K; running time versus M; theoretical complexity orders (p. 8-11).
complexity: O(1/2 R L h^2 M K) complex multiplications; Table II compares higher orders of three optimization baselines; running time about 0.2% of baselines at M=8 (p. 8-10).
q1_support: p. 3: "we consider the commonly adopted Saleh-Valenzuela channel model [9], [46]"; a custom simulated channel, with no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured data.
q2_support: p. 11: "the BGNN trained with variable M achieves satisfactory performance under different values of M"; the tested M (4-8) and K (3-7) are the values drawn in training (Algorithm 1, p. 8), and no unseen K, M, N or channel model is tested.
q3_support: p. 9: "we also consider a conventional DNN as a baseline" (learned) next to SDP-AltMin [10], MM-AltMin [12] and Element-AltMax [18] (non-learned); all compared on sum rate (p. 10-11).
q4_support: p. 8: "we can express the overall computational complexity of the proposed BGNN as" O(1/2 R L h^2 M K); p. 10: "The running time ratio of the proposed BGNN to the benchmark algorithms is around 0.2% when M = 8".
q5_support: p. 8: "Independently generate Ns channel matrices" in Algorithm 1 shows that the data are simulated; the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public dataset.
notes: Included as area 3 (hybrid beamforming of a MISO downlink). Scalability covers K and M only, since the operator sizes depend on N (Table I, p. 9). q2: the scalability tests in Figs. 7-8 (p. 11) train over M in {4..8} or K in {3..7} and test at the same values, so I did not count them as new conditions; the reviewer may weigh the paper's generalization claim. The conventional DNN counts as the learned baseline as a standard fully connected network applied to the same problem (p. 9).
